question: What nitrogenous base always pairs with adenine in a DNA molecule?
explanation: Adenine always bonds specifically with thymine in DNA base pairing to maintain the stability of the double helix structure. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the main job of the base sequence inside a DNA molecule?

options.A: Transporting energy molecules across the cell
options.B: Regulating the overall temperature of the cell
options.C: Providing structural support to the nuclear membrane
options.D: Instructing cells on how to build specific proteins

explanation: Think of DNA as a master recipe book! The specific order of bases acts as the exact code your body uses to build proteins. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h1)

question: How many total chromosomes are normally found in a human somatic cell?
explanation: Human body cells contain 46 chromosomes organized into 23 pairs, inheriting one set of 23 from each parent. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h2)

question: What do we call alternative forms of the same gene that lead to different traits, like eye color?
explanation: Alleles are just different versions of the same gene. They are the reason we all look unique! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h2)

question: Which type of allele needs two identical copies to show up as a physical trait in a person?
explanation: Recessive traits are shy! They get masked by dominant alleles, so you need to inherit two copies for the trait to show. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h3)

question: If both parents are healthy carriers of an autosomal recessive disorder, what is the chance they will have a child with the condition?
explanation: Every time carrier parents have a baby, there's a 1 in 4 (25%) chance the baby will inherit the faulty gene from both of them. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h3)

question: Which blood group system is a classic example of codominance, where both traits show equally?
explanation: In the AB blood group, neither A nor B hides the other—they both proudly show up together on the red blood cells! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why are males more likely to inherit X-linked recessive disorders than females?

options.A: They lack the cellular enzymes required to repair DNA damage.
options.B: Their Y chromosome actively triggers spontaneous genetic deletions.
options.C: X chromosomes duplicate at twice the normal rate in male embryos.
options.D: They possess only a single X chromosome without a backup copy.

explanation: Since guys only have one X chromosome (XY), they don't have a second X to rescue them if a recessive fault shows up on it. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h4)

question: What mistake during cell division causes a person to end up with an abnormal number of chromosomes?
explanation: Nondisjunction happens when chromosome pairs fail to separate neatly during cell division, leaving one cell with too many and another with too few. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h5)

question: What do we call an environmental factor, like UV rays or tobacco, that can permanently change DNA?
explanation: Mutagens are things in our environment (like radiation or harsh chemicals) that can mess with our DNA sequence. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h5)

question: Down syndrome is caused by which specific chromosomal abnormality?
explanation: You've got this! Down syndrome happens when there are three copies of chromosome 21 instead of the usual pair. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the main physical problem caused by the genetic defect in cystic fibrosis?

options.A: Thick, sticky mucus secretions in the lungs and digestive tract
options.B: Rapid uncontrolled proliferation of abnormal white blood cells
options.C: Inability to metabolize specific amino acids causing brain damage
options.D: Destruction of red blood cells leading to severe chronic jaundice

explanation: Cystic fibrosis messes with how salt and water move across cells, making body secretions super thick and clogging up airways and ducts. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the main reason a nurse draws a pedigree chart during an assessment?

options.A: To measure the concentration of circulating blood proteins
options.B: To calculate the precise metabolic rate of a pregnant patient
options.C: To map out family health history and spot inherited risks
options.D: To track daily vital signs in patients with chronic respiratory illnesses

explanation: A pedigree chart is basically a medical family tree. It helps you quickly spot patterns of diseases running in the family! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which action best shows the nurse's role when dealing with genetic health concerns?

options.A: Telling the family which reproductive choices they must make
options.B: Referring high-risk families to professional genetic counseling services
options.C: Making final decisions regarding whether a patient should undergo testing
options.D: Interpreting complex DNA sequencing data independently without specialists

explanation: As a nurse, you spot the red flags in family history and connect patients to the experts who can guide them best! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h7)
